summary: Usage Today bar shows '0/100' for Pro — denominator is the runaway-loop guard, not a real cap
description:
The /account "Usage Today" section renders {used} / {limit} from /api/quota.
For Pro users, /api/quota returns query_limit = PRO_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT (100),
which is a soft runaway-loop guard — NOT the user's actual cap. Pro is
gated on PRO_DAILY_USD_CAP, which translates to ~2 to ~27 queries/day
depending on provider (per /settings). Showing "0 / 100" misleads Pro
users about both their headroom and what their cap actually is.

Free users have a real query-count cap (FREE_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT = 10),
so the {used} / {limit} display is correct for them.

Fix:

  - Free tier: keep "{used} / {limit}" with the progress bar. Limit
    is real and binding.

  - Pro tier: drop the denominator. Show "{used} today" only, and
    hide the progress bar (or render it at 0% — there's no meaningful
    fill ratio to show without a real cap). Pro users get their real
    per-provider cap from /settings, where it already lives.

  - The /api/quota endpoint stays unchanged. The 100 still serves its
    purpose server-side as a runaway-loop guard; we just stop
    rendering it as if it were the user's quota.

Done when:
  - Pro users see "0 today" or similar (no /100), no fill bar
    suggesting a denominator.
  - Free users see "0 / 10" with the bar (unchanged behavior).
  - Source-level test guards both shapes.
  - tsc + lint + build clean.

Spec: live user feedback after the rest of the pre-launch cleanup
landed on chore/pre-launch-cleanup-tickets.

resolution.test_function: Pro renders a count-only label, never with the runaway-loop denominator
resolution.note: Pro Usage Today renders count-only ("0 today"); progress bar hidden. Free unchanged. 259 tests pass; tsc + lint clean.
